claims.claim: Albemarle links lithium resources and chemical conversion to batteries and electrification; its structural leverage is strongest where low-cost resource access can be converted economically into qualified battery-grade material.
Kemerton's idling shows the successor bottleneck is not lithium availability alone but competitive conversion cost, utilization and geography-specific operating economics.

causalEdges: electrification/battery demand -> lithium chemical demand -> resource extraction/conversion -> battery supply
resource scale -> potential cost/supply resilience -> customer availability
high conversion cost -> plant idling -> reduced downstream footprint
falsifiers: Sustained lithium oversupply keeps prices below levels required for attractive returns despite volume growth.
Conversion assets remain structurally uncompetitive even when lithium prices recover.
unknowns: full-year free cash flow across lithium-price scenarios

claims.claim: Improving lithium conditions alongside Kemerton idling is material evidence that commodity recovery does not automatically repair downstream conversion economics.
Cost and balance-sheet actions improve resilience, but cash generation remains price-sensitive and prior cash flow benefited from a one-time customer prepayment.

contradictions.contradiction: Lithium conditions improved, yet Kemerton economics remained insufficient to keep Train 1 operating.

unknowns: full-year free cash flow across lithium-price scenarios
